body:
Test runs, full gates and host credit. The rules are CLAUDE.md ("Shared test launcher", "Failed gate investigation", "Engram work tracker") and docs/test.md; this holds the traps and practices around them. Item-bound workarounds: live-workarounds.

TEST OUTPUT AND WAITING (Greg's preference, 2026-09-19, clarified 2026-09-22 via Engram::Advisor mailbox #131, for TermAl and Engram)
- Keep every required test; filter only output entering model context. Capture full stdout/stderr to per-gate disk logs, preserving native exit status independently.
- The model receives a compact terminal PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN summary with exit code (totals optional) plus bounded actual failures/warnings, full-log locators and explicit truncation notices. No streaming/tee, passing-test lists, or reading successful logs merely to confirm success; never use a blind error-word search as the verdict. Runner exception/crash or missing completion evidence is failure/unknown, never empty PASS.
- Announce once, use existing process completion/notification and yield; no sleep/status-poll/log-tail or acknowledgement ping-pong loops, no duplicate runs to regain visibility. If a supported execution wait yields, resume the same execution, not a new run.
- Diagnose and classify failures, preserve evidence, fix within already authorized scope and run required validation without an extra parent-approval round trip; no automatic unchanged retry-until-green and no claiming that a rerun pass alone proves a causal fix. Do not interrupt or repeat active tests just to apply reporting changes. .claude/commands/review-changes.md already defines disk logs, bounded diagnostics, exit preservation and completion-driven waiting; reuse it rather than duplicating. Scope/Git/deploy limits remain unchanged.

RUNNING FULL GATES
- No turn-taking (paraphrases of Greg, 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-27, from Engram memories): Engram and TermAl do not take turns for Cargo or Node runs, nor coordinate heavy runs (full gates, scale tests, release builds); each builds into its own target directory. Overlapping gates and builds should not cause failures; overlap is not an accepted excuse for flakiness.
- Start a full gate when its input is frozen. Send the coordinator one line at start and one at end, with the run directory, so a failure can be checked against an overlap. Do not hold a gate, reserve a window or send START/RELEASE handshakes. Disclose a review pair's start and end, so its CPU load is no surprise; nobody blocks on it.
- A failure during an overlap is still investigated as a defect. Never attribute a stall to the other project without measured timestamps from it. Contention can falsify a time-based measurement (a timing, a deadline): repeat it; counter-based results (counts, sums, decodes) cannot move. Before a long run, name which assertions contention could reach. Longer wall time alone is not a signal; a passing run gets no load narrative.
- Launch the launcher in a Bash call of its own, with an absolute path, never alongside another Bash call: the calls share one working directory (a run once reported PASS for an input it never saw). Never build two checkouts into one CARGO_TARGET_DIR without `cargo clean -p termal` first: Cargo's mtime check can run master's stale binary and still PASS, because the launcher fingerprints the source tree, not the binary.
- Before trusting a PASS: read the run's input.json (root and diff hash), check that rust-tests.log shows `Compiling termal (<the tree you meant>)`, and compare the test count with the previous run.
- During a gate do not edit code or tests: a result belongs to the binary that produced it. When an unknown process appears, capture its command line and start time at once.

EARNING HOST CREDIT
- Recognised (src/engram_check_recognition.rs, master d705038): `npx vitest ...`, `cargo test ...`, `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs ...` (focused only when its inner command is recognised too). Silently unrecognised (no record, no refusal line): `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ...`; `node --test ...`; a focused launcher run that prints no passing count; any multi-line command (a test on a later line is never seen; w-8468e1f2efdf). So run every credited check as one single-line command, cwd in the named root (or its ui/ for Vitest), no environment prefix. Claude: `pushd "DIR" && <test>`.
- Never run a shell command (PowerShell, Bash, cargo, git, node) with its cwd inside another session's named worktree, even a read-only one: it fences that worktree's carried gate. This binds architects, reviewers and the coordinator alike. Inspect only with tools that run no process there (Read, Grep, Glob), or `git show <rev>:<path>` from your own cwd. Read-only review children run in their own workdir; their holder must not have a carried gate in the same root while they run.
- Your own carried gate (observed; holds until the host changes the behaviour): Claude's Bash tool keeps its cwd, so after 'pushd "DIR" && node scripts/test-launcher.mjs full --detach --notify …' (nothing chained, so no popd) every later Bash command starts in the worktree and is attributed there, even one starting 'cd /c/github/Personal/TermAl && …'; a cd or any not-purely-read-only command refuses the credit. Practice: run no Bash command at all until the record lands; use MCP tools and the PowerShell tool (its cwd stays at the repository root). The first Bash command after the record may start in the worktree harmlessly. Start no subagent while your gate is carried: its commands count as the session's and it starts in the session's cwd.
- Until w-10eafa34c480 is fixed (from 2026-09-29; drop when done), Termal::Codex runs bound checks for items held by Claude sessions: an evaluator does not take a Claude-run check as a passed host verification.
- Why no credit: `engram work show WORK_REF --note RECORD_LOCATOR` (`--json`: `verification` {result, check_kind, source_revision, producer_outcome, meaning}) prints the typed result, check kind, source revision, producer outcome, and each obligation with whether the record matches and the first mismatch. Indeterminate with producer outcome unknown means the HOST sent it as unknown: TermAl's side (overlap with another writer, no passing test shown, as in any focused launcher run, or a background run), not Engram's. Passed but matching no obligation names the refusing rule (source revision, position, time, claim). Read this before asking the Engram project. Evaluators do not see the typed result yet (w-67e7b8bdcade).

EVIDENCE FOR EVALUATION
- A non-holder's note is not current-run evidence. When a criterion rests on someone else's record, the holder adds a note citing it by locator or delegation id and quoting it, then asks for the evaluation.
- Write evidence an evaluator must read as notes of 600 characters or fewer that cite a file path and its sha256; the evaluator brief cuts longer notes (w-1ec7bb8b9caa).

FIXTURES AND REAL PRODUCERS (Fable2, 2026-10-02: a change passed 14 rounds, a credited gate and 7/7 evaluation, yet rejected the real producer's states)
(1) Check a host-side validator of an Engram wire enum against the producer's real enum (Engram src/domain/...), not the fixture's values. (2) Scripted fixtures emit every state the producer emits for the scenario (a claimed item reports claimed/active), or the test says which states it covers. (3) Before landing a change to an Engram contract path, run at least one real-store (live) check of the main path, or name in the review brief why it can't be run.

FAIL-FIRST CRITERIA (Fable2, 2026-10-03; it recurred on w-904fddc5961a, w-8f9988de4cb3 and w-a2d34cc16987): never bind a fail-first criterion to test. A test-bound criterion passes only on a host-recorded PASSED check, and a fail-first is a failing run, so a bound fail-first can never pass (w-a2d34's evaluation 2c5887a0 found it insufficient for exactly this reason). Leave it unbound and judge it on the failed host verification plus a holder note that cites the diagnostic run. Bind only the fix criteria and the full-gate criterion.
